name: JMdict
licenseNote: Cited from EDRDG's own project page, not freshly re-read this session. Confirm exact licence text at licenseUrl before shipping attribution copy.
purpose: Japanese-English dictionary: headwords, readings, senses, glosses, part-of-speech and register tags. Backs the app's dictionary/search feature (currently unbuilt).
format: XML, DOCTYPE with internal custom entities for POS/tag abbreviations (e.g. &n;, &v5k;) — a plain XML parser will fail on these unless the DOCTYPE internal subset is parsed too or entities are pre-expanded.

name: KANJIDIC2
licenseNote: Same EDRDG licence family as JMdict; not freshly re-read this session.
purpose: Per-kanji meanings, on/kun readings, radical, stroke count, grade level, JLPT-era legacy level tag, dictionary cross-references. Enriches (does not replace) the curated KanjiEntry seed content.
format: XML, well-formed, standard entities only (no custom DOCTYPE entities — simpler to parse than JMdict).

name: KRADFILE / RADKFILE
licenseNote: Same EDRDG licence family; not freshly re-read this session.
purpose: Kanji-to-radical-component decomposition (kradfile/kradfile2) and the reverse radical-to-kanji lookup (radkfile/radkfile2/radkfilex). Backs a component/radical kanji search.
format: Plain text, EUC-JP encoded (NOT UTF-8 — confirmed via `file`, 2026-08-13). Must be transcoded before parsing; a UTF-8 read will mangle every Japanese character.

name: KanjiVG
licenseNote: Read directly from the source file header: 'Copyright (C) 2009-2013 Ulrich Apel. This work is distributed under the conditions of the Creative Commons Attribution-Share Alike 3.0 Licence.' The packaged derivative preserves each SVG viewBox and stroke path geometry, orders paths by the source stroke-number IDs, and omits grouping/annotation metadata.
purpose: Deterministic stroke-order paths for every kana and kanji character taught by the authored curriculum.
format: Compact JSON derived from per-character SVG/XML: Unicode character, original viewBox, and path d values ordered by the source -sN stroke IDs.
recordCountMethod: Exact authored-character inventory verified by npm run verify:content, 2026-08-16

name: BCCWJ Short-Unit Word Frequency List
licenseNote: NOT freshly re-read this session. NINJAL's terms are for research/educational use — do not treat as cleared for commercial redistribution until the exact terms are re-read from licenseUrl. Use for internal frequency ranking only until then; do not expose raw BCCWJ figures as a bulk downloadable dataset from this app.
purpose: Corpus frequency rank per lemma, short-unit segmentation. Enriches vocab with frequencyRank for sorting/prioritization — not a source of definitions or examples.
format: TSV, header row, 76 columns (rank/frequency/pmw broken out per BCCWJ register subcorpus). Only rank/lemma/pos/frequency/pmw and the 'core' columns are likely needed — do not import all 76 columns verbatim.

name: BCCWJ Long-Unit Word Frequency List
purpose: Same as bccwj-suw but long-unit segmentation (captures compounds). Larger and noisier; suw is the better default join key against JMdict lemmas, luw is optional enrichment.
format: TSV, same column shape as bccwj-suw.

name: Tatoeba Japanese sentences
licenseNote: Confirmed via the cloned reference tool's README (data/raw/tatoeba/tatoeba-json/README.md), which itself cites Tatoeba's terms. Attribution is per-sentence and satisfiable with a permalink https://tatoeba.org/en/sentences/show/<id> — the sentence ID must be retained on every imported row for this reason; do not strip it after import.
format: TSV: id, lang, text. No header row.

name: Tatoeba English sentences
purpose: Example-sentence text, English side — joined to jpn_sentences via jpn_indices' sentence-id pairs.
format: TSV: id, lang, text. No header row. Whole file is ~2M rows across all uses of English on Tatoeba — only the subset referenced by jpn_indices.csv is relevant here; the importer must filter, not bulk-load.

name: Tatoeba/Tanaka Corpus Japanese indices
licenseNote: Same licence family as the sentence files; this is the Tanaka Corpus word-alignment layer integrated into Tatoeba.
purpose: THE join table: pairs a Japanese sentence ID with its English translation ID, plus a per-word annotation string (headword, reading, JMdict sense index, surface form, 'checked' flag). This is what makes 'example sentences for word X, with a verified sense match' possible — a bare sentence corpus without this cannot be reliably attached to a specific dictionary sense.
format: TSV: jpn_sentence_id, eng_sentence_id, annotation_string. Annotation format documented at https://www.edrdg.org/~jwb/paperdir/dicexamples.html (Tanaka Corpus format) — read that before writing the annotation parser, the bracket/brace syntax is not self-explanatory.
